This study describes a new contactless monitoring device (DUiFK-P) for cardiovascular assessment, not trans-thoracic Doppler echocardiography for PH detection. No RHC reference standard is used, and the study does not evaluate diagnostic accuracy for PH.

This study only includes patients WITH pulmonary hypertension (160+23 consecutive PH patients), representing a one-gate/case-only design. There is no control group of patients without PH, so specificity cannot be calculated. The study uses Bland-Altman analysis for agreement rather than providing TP/FP/TN/FN data for diagnostic accuracy.
This is a guideline/recommendation document providing updated normal values for cardiac chambers, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. It does not evaluate TTE for PH detection against RHC.

This appears to be an editorial/commentary discussing another study rather than a primary diagnostic accuracy study. It references 'the article' and discusses limitations of another investigation. No original diagnostic accuracy data is presented.

This study evaluates TTE (Doppler calculation of RVSP and PVR) against RHC in 100 patients. While the abstract focuses on correlation/agreement, it assesses diagnostic accuracy of echocardiographic methods for estimating pulmonary pressures. Full-text may provide extractable 2x2 data. Conservative approach warrants inclusion.

This study evaluates echocardiographic parameters (TAPSE/RVSP ratio) for identifying PH using RHC as reference standard with mPAP ≥25mmHg threshold. ROC analysis with AUC=0.80 is reported, suggesting diagnostic accuracy data exists. Full-text may allow extraction of TP/FP/TN/FN values.

This is a prognostic study examining the association between PASP assessed by Doppler echocardiography and mortality in heart failure patients. It does not use RHC as reference standard and does not evaluate diagnostic accuracy for PH detection.

This study uses a PH definition threshold of mean PAP >20 mmHg (per newer guidelines), which differs from the required 25 mmHg threshold specified in the selection criteria. Although it uses RHC as reference and provides sensitivity/specificity, the threshold mismatch excludes it.

This study evaluates Doppler echocardiography against RHC with mPAP ≥25 mmHg threshold. Clear diagnostic accuracy data provided: 24/49 had PH by RHC, echo classified 38 correctly (14/24 with PH = TP, 24/25 without PH = TN). This allows extraction of TP=14, FN=10, TN=24, FP=1.

This study evaluates CW and PW Doppler echocardiography against RHC in 72 patients (43 with PH, 27 without). While the abstract emphasizes correlation, it reports PPV of 84% for AcT<90 msec, indicating diagnostic accuracy assessment. Full-text may provide extractable 2x2 data.

This study compares different formulas for calculating PASP using Doppler gradient + RA pressure estimates. It reports correlation coefficients (r values) and SEE, but does not provide diagnostic accuracy data (TP/FP/TN/FN) for detecting PH. Focus is on formula comparison, not diagnostic accuracy.

This study evaluates pulmonary venous flow parameters for estimating LEFT VENTRICULAR END-DIASTOLIC PRESSURE (LVEDP), not for detecting pulmonary hypertension. The outcome of interest is different from the review question.

This study defines pulmonary arterial hypertension as PAPs ≥35 mmHg, which differs from the required 25 mmHg threshold. Although it uses RHC as reference and evaluates Doppler echocardiography, the threshold mismatch excludes it per selection criteria.

This diagnostic test study evaluates TDI parameter (TTP) against RHC with correct threshold (mPAP <25 vs ≥25 mmHg). Sensitivity and specificity of ~70% are reported with AUC=0.746. Full-text should allow extraction of TP/FP/TN/FN values.

This study focuses on MONITORING hemodynamic deterioration over time (>10% increase in PASP) rather than initial DIAGNOSIS of PH. All 69 patients already have CTD-associated PAH. The objective is predicting deterioration, not detecting PH presence/absence.

This study evaluates ECG, NT-proBNP, SO2, and WHO functional class - NOT trans-thoracic Doppler echocardiography. While RHC is used as reference, the index test is different from what the review seeks to evaluate.

This study reports correlation (rho=0.79) between echo and RHC measurements but does not provide diagnostic accuracy data (TP/FP/TN/FN) for detecting PH. It focuses on correlation rather than classification accuracy.

This study defines clinically significant PH as PASP >50 mmHg, which differs from the required 25 mmHg threshold. Although it uses RHC as reference and evaluates Doppler echocardiography, the threshold mismatch excludes it per selection criteria.

This study evaluates multiple Doppler echocardiographic parameters (TR peak velocity, TR mean gradient, pulmonary acceleration time) against RHC. Sensitivity and specificity values are reported (e.g., sensitivity 0.85, specificity 0.5 for PAPm from acceleration time). Full-text should allow extraction of TP/FP/TN/FN values.

This study compares characteristics and identifies predictors of PH in emphysema patients. It reports demographics, pulmonary function variables, and multivariate analysis results, but does not evaluate diagnostic accuracy of TTE against RHC with TP/FP/TN/FN data.

Study evaluates diagnostic accuracy of Doppler echocardiography vs RHC (reference standard). Reports sensitivity (85%), specificity (67%), PPV (87%), NPV (61%) - sufficient data to extract 2x2 table. Population is adults (lung transplant candidates).

While RHC is used as reference and Doppler ultrasound is evaluated, the abstract only reports correlation coefficient (r=0.93) without sensitivity, specificity, or 2x2 table data. Insufficient diagnostic accuracy data to extract TP, FP, TN, FN values.

Study evaluates diagnostic accuracy of Doppler echocardiography vs RHC (reference standard). PH defined as mean PAP ≥25 mmHg (correct threshold). Reports sensitivity (82.2%), specificity (80.2%), PPV (83.1%), NPV (79.2%) - sufficient data to extract 2x2 table.

While RHC is used as reference and echocardiographic criteria are evaluated, only specificity and PPV are reported for various indices. Sensitivity and NPV are not provided, making it impossible to extract complete 2x2 table data.
Abstract only contains conclusions without methods or results. No diagnostic accuracy data (sensitivity, specificity, or 2x2 table) is reported. Insufficient information to assess eligibility.

While RHC is used as reference and Doppler echocardiography is evaluated, only Bland-Altman analysis and inaccuracy rates are reported. No sensitivity, specificity, or 2x2 table data provided to extract TP, FP, TN, FN values.

While RHC is used as reference and Doppler echocardiography is evaluated, only correlation coefficients and PASP differences are reported. No sensitivity, specificity, or 2x2 table data provided to extract TP, FP, TN, FN values.
Study focuses on predicting pulmonary wedge pressure (PAWP), not on detecting pulmonary hypertension. Wrong outcome measure - does not evaluate diagnostic accuracy for PH detection.

While RHC is used as reference and Doppler echocardiography is evaluated, only correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analysis are reported. No sensitivity, specificity, or 2x2 table data provided to extract TP, FP, TN, FN values.

While RHC is used as reference and Doppler ultrasound is evaluated, only correlation coefficient (r=0.97) is reported. No sensitivity, specificity, or 2x2 table data provided to extract TP, FP, TN, FN values.
Descriptive study analyzing causes of PH in elderly patients. Not a diagnostic accuracy study evaluating echocardiography vs RHC. Wrong study type.

While catheterization is used as reference and Doppler echocardiography is evaluated, only correlation coefficients are reported. No sensitivity, specificity, or 2x2 table data provided to extract TP, FP, TN, FN values.

While RHC is used as reference and Doppler echocardiography is evaluated, only PPV (39%) and NPV (90%) are reported. Sensitivity and specificity are not provided, making it impossible to extract complete 2x2 table data.

Study evaluates TTE probability algorithm vs RHC (reference standard). PH defined as mPAP ≥25mmHg (correct threshold). Reports sensitivity (89%) and specificity (68%) - sufficient data to extract 2x2 table.
Study evaluates prediction of SEVERE PH (PASP ≥61 mmHg), not PH detection at the standard 25 mmHg threshold. Different reference standard threshold than required by protocol.
Methodological paper on meta-analysis techniques for diagnostic test accuracy. Not a primary diagnostic accuracy study evaluating echocardiography for PH detection. Wrong study type.
Appears to be a review or commentary article discussing noninvasive diagnosis of PH. No primary diagnostic accuracy data reported. Wrong study type.

Study evaluates echocardiography parameters vs RHC (reference standard). PH defined as mean PAP ≥25 mmHg (correct threshold). Reports sensitivity (89%, 84%), specificity (63%, 69%), NPV (78%, 68%), PPV (80%, 84%) - sufficient data to extract 2x2 table.
Consensus statement on diastolic heart failure diagnosis. Not a diagnostic accuracy study for PH detection. Wrong topic.
Protocol paper describing a proposed screening algorithm. No primary diagnostic accuracy data reported. Wrong study type.

Study evaluates Doppler echo accuracy for pressure estimation using RHC as reference, but focuses on continuous pressure agreement (Bland-Altman analysis) rather than binary PH classification. Does not report TP/FP/TN/FN or sensitivity/specificity for PH detection at 25 mmHg threshold.
Study focuses on estimating pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR), not on detecting pulmonary hypertension. Different outcome measure than the review objective.
Two-gate design: compares liver transplant patients (n=31) with a separate control group (n=49). This violates the exclusion criterion for diagnostic case-control studies (two-gate design).

Evaluates diagnostic accuracy of echocardiography for PH detection using RHC as reference standard. Compares multiple algorithms for identifying PH. While specific TP/FP/TN/FN not reported in abstract, odds ratios and accuracy comparisons suggest extractable data. Conservative inclusion recommended.
Study defines severe PH as MPAP >45 mmHg, not the required 25 mmHg threshold. Also appears to use single-gate design (only patients with PH). Does not meet selection criteria.
Uses mean pulmonary artery pressure >20 mmHg as threshold, not the required 25 mmHg. Does not report sufficient diagnostic test accuracy data (TP/FP/TN/FN).

Compares three Doppler methods against cardiac catheterization for predicting pulmonary artery pressure. While abstract truncated, study design suggests potential for extracting diagnostic accuracy data. Conservative inclusion recommended.

Cohort study comparing echocardiography with RHC for PH diagnosis in lung transplant candidates. Reports sensitivity (85%), specificity (55%), PPV (52%), and NPV (87%). Data allows extraction of TP/FP/TN/FN values. Meets selection criteria.
Study focuses on detecting occult diastolic dysfunction, not pulmonary hypertension. Different target condition than the review objective.

Evaluates diagnostic ability of echocardiography to detect PH using RHC as reference with correct threshold (mPAP >25 mmHg). Reports likelihood ratios that can be converted to TP/FP/TN/FN. Meets selection criteria.
Population-based prevalence study using only echocardiography without RHC as reference standard. Does not evaluate diagnostic accuracy against the gold standard.

Predicts PH (mPAP≥25mmHg on RHC) using alternative echo parameters. Reports AU-ROC, sensitivity (95%, 96%), and specificity (33%, 40%). Data allows extraction of TP/FP/TN/FN. Meets selection criteria.
Study about IL-6 for sepsis diagnosis, completely unrelated to pulmonary hypertension or echocardiography. Wrong topic entirely.

Assesses accuracy of echocardiography-based formulas to estimate mPAP (≥25 mmHg) against RHC in lung transplant patients. Strong correlations reported (rs=0.909, rs=0.904). While TP/FP/TN/FN not explicitly stated, data may be extractable. Conservative inclusion recommended.
Treatment algorithm/guideline document, not a diagnostic accuracy study. Does not evaluate diagnostic test performance.
Methodological systematic review about search filters for DTA studies, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study of echocardiography for PH.
Uses PAP ≥20 mmHg as threshold for PH definition, not the required 25 mmHg. Does not meet selection criteria for reference standard threshold.
Very small number of patients with both DE and RHC (n=15), poor correlation (r=-0.29). Does not provide sufficient diagnostic test accuracy data for meaningful analysis.

Evaluates accuracy of Doppler echocardiography-estimated PASP compared with RHC in HIV patients. Reports inaccuracy rate (19.7%) and miss rate (one-third). While TP/FP/TN/FN not explicitly stated, data may be extractable. Conservative inclusion recommended.

Focuses on correlation between noninvasive and invasive pressure measurements (r=0.97, r=0.96) without evaluating binary PH detection. Does not report TP/FP/TN/FN or sensitivity/specificity for PH diagnosis.

Study reports only correlation coefficients (r=0.97, 0.87, 0.80) between Doppler and catheterization measurements. No diagnostic accuracy data (TP, FP, TN, FN) or sensitivity/specificity values provided.
Study evaluates detection of increased PVR (>3 Woods units) and uses PASP>40 mmHg threshold, not mPAP≥25 mmHg. Reference standard threshold differs from required 25 mmHg.
This is a review article discussing MR and CT imaging for PH evaluation, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study of Doppler echocardiography.
Cross-sectional study in IPF patients. Reports that 40% of ECHOs accurately reflected PAP but does not provide TP/FP/TN/FN values or clear sensitivity/specificity data extractable from abstract.
Abstract describes SWEDEHEART registry characteristics, not a diagnostic accuracy study. Title does not match abstract content.
Review article about riociguat treatment for PH, not a diagnostic accuracy study of echocardiography.
Two-gate design with separate study group (liver transplant candidates) and control group (no liver disease). Only reports correlation coefficient (R=0.58), no TP/FP/TN/FN data.

Prospective single-gate study in MS patients. Uses RHC as reference standard. Reports sensitivity (92.8%) and specificity (86.6%) for sPAP(TRVmax) in detecting PH. Data allows extraction of TP/FP/TN/FN.
MRI myocardial tagging study investigating interventricular asynchrony in PAH patients. Not a diagnostic accuracy study of Doppler echocardiography.
Primary index test is phase contrast MRI, not Doppler echocardiography. Echocardiography is compared but not the main focus of diagnostic accuracy evaluation.
Single-gate study with RHC as reference standard. Uses mPAP≥25 mmHg threshold. Reports AUC=0.92 for noninvasive sPAP to predict invasively assessed mPAP≥25 mmHg. Diagnostic accuracy data available.
Single-gate study in lung transplant candidates. Uses RHC with mPAP≥25 mmHg threshold. Reports sensitivity (92.3%), specificity (81.8%), AUC (0.84) for RVSP≥43 mmHg. TP/FP/TN/FN extractable.
Uses SPAP≥30 mmHg threshold for screening, not mPAP≥25 mmHg. Reference standard threshold differs from required 25 mmHg.
Two-gate design (Group 1: RVsys≥50 mmHg had elective RHC; Group 2: RVsys<50 mmHg had pressures measured during transplant). Uses MPAP≥35 mmHg threshold, not 25 mmHg.
Cross-sectional study with RHC as reference standard. Reports sensitivity (81%) and specificity (69%) at RVSP>52 mmHg cutoff for predicting PH. TP/FP/TN/FN can be extracted from these values.
Registry study examining demographics, epidemiology, and survival of incident PAH. Not a diagnostic accuracy study of echocardiography.
Prognostic study deriving survival prediction equation from REVEAL registry. Not a diagnostic accuracy study of echocardiography.
Reports only correlation coefficients (r=0.71, 0.85, 0.83, 0.92) between echo-Doppler parameters and mPAP. No TP/FP/TN/FN or sensitivity/specificity data provided.
Title mentions PH but abstract describes cardiac resynchronization therapy and mechanical dyssynchrony assessment. Not a diagnostic accuracy study of echocardiography for PH.
Investigates relationship between PA distensibility and RV ejection pattern. Reports correlations but no diagnostic accuracy data (TP/FP/TN/FN) for PH detection.

Study evaluates echocardiography for PAH detection in IPF patients using RHC as reference standard, but does not provide sufficient TP, FP, TN, FN data - only reports AUC (0.72) without 2x2 table data.
This is a registry study examining factors associated with delayed PAH recognition, not a diagnostic accuracy study evaluating echocardiography against RHC.

Study evaluates Doppler echocardiography vs RHC for PH detection with correct 25 mmHg threshold, but does not provide sufficient TP, FP, TN, FN data - only reports correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analysis.
This study examines the effectiveness of RHC in critically ill patients, not the diagnostic accuracy of echocardiography for PH detection.
Study uses sPAP cutoff of 36 mmHg rather than the required mPAP ≥25 mmHg threshold for defining PH. The reference standard threshold differs from 25 mmHg.

Study evaluates Doppler methods for right ventricular afterload assessment using RHC as reference, but does not provide sufficient TP, FP, TN, FN data - only reports correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analysis.

Study evaluates Doppler echocardiography for portopulmonary hypertension detection using cardiac catheterization as reference standard with mPAP ≥25 mmHg threshold. Provides sensitivity (100%), specificity (88%), and PPV (30%) from which TP, FP, TN, FN can be calculated. Single-gate design with all 107 patients undergoing both tests.
This is a methodological paper describing the QUADAS-2 tool for quality assessment, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study evaluating echocardiography for PH detection.
Study focuses on right atrial pressure (RAP) estimation accuracy, not on PH detection. The outcome measure differs from the review objective of detecting PH.
This is a clinical classification guideline document, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study evaluating echocardiography for PH detection.

Study evaluates echocardiographic parameters (PR gradient and PAT) for PH detection using RHC as reference standard with mPAP ≥25 mmHg threshold. Provides sensitivity (60.8%) and specificity (82.4%) for PAT from which TP, FP, TN, FN can be calculated. Single-gate design with 353 consecutive patients.

Study evaluates echocardiographic accuracy for PA pressure estimation using RHC as reference, but does not provide sufficient TP, FP, TN, FN data - only reports bias and limits of agreement from Bland-Altman analysis.
This is a review article summarizing existing literature on Doppler diagnosis of PH, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.

Study uses a two-gate (case-control) design where only patients with suspected PAH on echocardiography (VTR >3 m/s or 2.5-3 m/s with dyspnea) underwent RHC. This violates the exclusion criterion for diagnostic case-control studies.
Abstract is too brief and does not provide sufficient information about study design, reference standard, or diagnostic accuracy data (TP, FP, TN, FN).

Study evaluates Doppler echocardiography for PAH detection in scleroderma patients using RHC as reference standard. Provides sensitivity (100%) and specificity (63.6%) for echocardiography from which TP, FP, TN, FN can be calculated. Single-gate design with all 15 patients undergoing both tests.

Study evaluates Doppler echocardiography for PH detection in ICU patients using RHC as reference standard with mPAP ≥25 mmHg threshold. Reports 100% sensitivity and specificity for sPAP >39 mmHg from which TP, FP, TN, FN can be calculated. Single-gate design with 40 patients.

Study evaluates echocardiography for PH detection in emphysema patients using RHC as reference standard. Provides sensitivity (60%), specificity (74%), PPV (68%), and NPV (67%) from which TP, FP, TN, FN can be calculated. Single-gate design with 74 paired measurements.

Study evaluates echocardiography for PH detection using RHC as reference standard with mPAP ≥25 mmHg threshold, but does not provide sufficient TP, FP, TN, FN data - only reports correlation coefficients.

Study evaluates Doppler echocardiography for PASP estimation using cardiac catheterization as reference, but does not provide sufficient TP, FP, TN, FN data - only reports correlation coefficients (r=0.96).
Uses incorrect PH threshold (SPAP >35 mmHg or mean pressure >20 mmHg instead of mPAP ≥25 mmHg). Does not provide explicit TP/FP/TN/FN values.
This is a review article about cardiac MRI, not a diagnostic accuracy study of trans-thoracic echocardiography. No diagnostic test accuracy data provided.
This is a clinical guideline document, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. No abstract available and no TP/FP/TN/FN data.
This is a meta-analysis/systematic review, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. While it summarizes data from other studies, it does not provide original TP/FP/TN/FN data from a single cohort.

While this study compares echo with RHC, it only reports correlation coefficients (r=0.47) without providing TP/FP/TN/FN values or sensitivity/specificity data needed for diagnostic accuracy analysis.
Uses incorrect PH thresholds (eco-PASP >32.5 mmHg for Chagas and >35.5 mmHg for non-Chagas instead of mPAP ≥25 mmHg). Also focuses on a specific transplant population.
Uses RHC as reference standard with correct mPAP >25 mmHg threshold. Provides sensitivity (89%) and specificity (84%) for AT cut-off of 100 ms. TP/FP/TN/FN can be extracted from these values.

Uses RHC as reference standard. Reports that 99 had PAH and 38 did not at catheterization. Provides PPV data (97% with TG >45 mmHg). While complete 2x2 table not explicitly stated, data may be extractable from full text.

Uses RHC as reference standard. Provides clear data: 17 met criteria on echo, 10 confirmed by cath (TP), 7 ruled out (FP), and states 'no false negatives' (FN=0). TN can be calculated from total n=165. TP/FP/TN/FN extractable.
Uses RHC as reference standard. Reports sensitivity (97%) and specificity (83%) for MPAP calculation detecting PH. With n=115 patients, TP/FP/TN/FN values can be calculated from these percentages.
Completely irrelevant topic - this study is about H. pylori infection diagnosis, not pulmonary hypertension or echocardiography.

Uses RHC as reference standard with correct mPAP ≥25 mmHg threshold. Provides specificity data (18.8% at TRV 2.51 m/s, 81% at TRV 2.88 m/s). With n=25 patients and 9 with mPAP≥25, TP/FP/TN/FN can be derived.

Uses RHC as reference standard with correct mPAP ≥25 mmHg threshold. Reports AUROC values for multiple formulae. With n=33 patients and ROC data, diagnostic accuracy data should be extractable from full text.
Abstract is truncated but title suggests relevant diagnostic accuracy study. States PH defined as mPAP ≥25 mmHg by RHC. Full text needed to confirm data availability.

Uses RHC as reference standard. Provides detailed data: 74 met criteria on echo at 30 mmHg cutoff, 7 confirmed by cath (TP=7, FP=67). At 38 mmHg cutoff, sensitivity=100%, specificity=82%. With n=152, TP/FP/TN/FN calculable.
Only conclusion available but indicates comparison between echo and RHC for PH quantification. Mentions 30% misclassification rate. Full text needed to extract complete diagnostic accuracy data.
This is a review article about emergency management protocols for PAH patients, not a diagnostic accuracy study of echocardiography. No TP/FP/TN/FN data.

Uses RHC as reference standard. Reports sensitivity (90.5%), specificity (80%), and accuracy (84.8%) for post-exercise TR velocity >3.4 m/s. Note: mentions mPAP >20 mmHg threshold which differs from protocol's 25 mmHg, but data may still be useful. With n=46, TP/FP/TN/FN calculable.

Uses RHC as reference standard with correct mPAP ≥25 mmHg threshold. Reports sensitivity (93%), specificity (67%), PPV (91%), NPV (73%). With n=64 patients and 77% having PH, TP/FP/TN/FN values can be calculated.
This is a methodological paper about statistical approaches for meta-analysis of diagnostic studies, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study of echocardiography for PH. No TP/FP/TN/FN data.
Meta-analysis synthesizing data from multiple studies; does not provide raw TP/FP/TN/FN from a single primary study population.
Uses logistic regression for PoPH prediction; no diagnostic accuracy metrics or 2x2 table reported.
Systematic review of predictors of hospitalization/mortality; not a diagnostic accuracy study.
Case-control (two-gate) design with separate PH and non-PH groups; evaluates composite clinical criteria, not TTE alone.
Uses 20 mmHg threshold for PH definition instead of required 25 mmHg.
Abstract is incomplete/truncated; insufficient information to assess eligibility.
Review article discussing test integration; no original diagnostic accuracy data.
Evaluates exercise pressure-flow relationships (≥3 mmHg/L/min threshold), not resting PH diagnosis at 25 mmHg.
Correlation study with only confirmed PH patients (no non-PH controls); cannot construct 2x2 table.
Prevalence study in SSc patients; does not evaluate diagnostic accuracy with TP/FP/TN/FN data.
Bland-Altman agreement study; mentions 10 non-PH patients but provides no 2x2 contingency table.
Prevalence/clinical correlates study of PH in patients without TRV; not a diagnostic accuracy study.
Evaluates PVR estimation by echo, not PH diagnosis; outcome is continuous PVR, not binary PH detection.

Meets all criteria: evaluates TTE diagnostic accuracy for PH using RHC at 25 mmHg threshold; reports sensitivity (88%), specificity (83%), accuracy (86%) with sample sizes allowing TP/FP/TN/FN extraction; single-gate design.
Evaluates PH severity grading (normal/moderate/high) rather than binary PH detection; no 2x2 table for 25 mmHg threshold.
